main_text.p: Cur aut quomodo utile & necessarium? Quia ideo institutum est à Deo, primùm, ne homo fit solus, sed habeat sociam & adjutricem conjunctam in tota vita, nec solùm in procreatione, sed etiam in educatione libe-rorum, in regenda familia, in parandis & tuendis rebus ad hanc vitam necessariis, ut partem laborum & molestiarum sustineat, & ut omnis fortunæ sociam, & quasi solatium & levamen multarum miseriarum hujus æ-rumnosæ vitæ habeat. Genef.2. Ecclef. 4.9. Neque enim in ærumnis remedium ullum suavius & dulcius est, quàm præsentia & confociatio piæ & prudentis conjugis: Sicuti & Proverb.31. dicitur: Cui contigit proba uxor, ea præstat gemmis, confidit ea cor mariti, & res familiaris non deficiet. Et Eccles.26. Mulier comis exhilarat maritum: & cùm humaniter eum tractat, recreat cor ejus. Item cap.37. Mulier formosa exhilarat maritum suum. Et cap.40. Ut amicus commodè congruat cum amico, vir tamen & uxor concordes utriq; præferendi sunt. Hinc Augustinus de bono Conjugali cap.3. ait: Quod (bonum conjugii bonum) mihi non videtur propter solam filiorum procreationem, sed propter ipsam naturalem in diverso sexu societatem. Alioqui non jam dicere-tur conjugium in senibus, præsertim si vel amississent filios, vel minimè genuissent. Nunc verò in bono licet annoso conjugio, etsi e-marcuit ardor ætatis inter masculum & fœ-

page.notes: Genef. and Ecclef. are printed with long-s forms; transcribed as Genes. and Eccles. per the rule on long s, with the printed forms kept in the text where they appear as abbreviations. Doubtful readings: "Alioqui" (accent unclear), "amississent" (the ss ligature is hard to read), "Genef.2." and "Eccles." as printed. Margin fragments at the far right edge are cut off and unreadable; they are not transcribed. The page number reads 451 as printed; the final digit is small and somewhat doubtful.
